paper.title_en: Hybrid compact stars with finite strange quark mass and dark energy: implications for astrophysical observations
paper.abstract_en: In this work, we present a detailed investigation of compact stars composed of deconfined quark matter, with finite strange quark mass ($m_s\neq0$), admixed with dark energy. The quark sector is described using the MIT bag model equation of state, while the dark energy component is assumed to satisfy a linear equation of state of the form $p^{de}=ωρ^{de}$, where $ω$ lies in the range $-1\leqω\leq-\frac{1}{3}$. The stellar configuration is studied within the Finch-Skea ansatz for the $g_{rr}$ metric potential. A coupling between the two components is introduced through the relation $ρ^{de}=βρ^Q$, where $β$ denotes the dark energy coupling parameter. From causality arguments, the admissible range of $β$ is constrained as $0<β<-\frac{1}{3ω}$. The structural properties of such compact stars are then analysed by varying $β$ within this range. Solution of the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations yields a maximum mass of $2.012~ M_{\odot}$ with a corresponding radius of $\approx 11$ km. Notably, for a fixed $ω$, both the stellar mass and radius are found to decrease with increasing $β$. The model is further examined through causality, energy, and stability conditions, all of which are satisfied, thereby ensuring physical viability. Finally, the framework is applied to estimate radii of several compact star candidates identified as strange quark stars admixed with dark energy, with predictions showing close agreement with recent observational results.
